headline: FIRST MINING'S MIROIR ZONE EXTENDS TO 220m STRIKE: 5.26 g/t Au OVER 19.55m AT DUPARQUET — OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
source_name: Streetwise Reports / First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF)
snippet: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) released results on September 10, 2026 from its 2026 drill program at the Duparquet Gold Project in Quebec's Abitibi, with Streetwise Reports providing analysis September 11. Hole DUP26-093 returned 5.26 g/t gold over 19.55 metres, including 7.58 g/t gold over 12.95 metres; hole DUP26-096 returned 3.43 g/t gold over 28.0 metres, with a 21.80 g/t gold high-grade sub-interval over 1.0 metre; DUP26-095 returned 3.36 g/t gold over 15.8 metres. All four holes successfully targeted a down-plunge and easterly extension of the Miroir zone, expanding its known strike length from approximately 150 metres to approximately 220 metres — and the zone remains open in all directions. First Mining commenced its 2026 drill program in May targeting 15,000 metres, focused on resource advancement at the Miroir discovery first identified in 2024. For investors tracking Abitibi gold: the Miroir zone at 220 metres of confirmed strike, 19–28 metre widths, and grades consistently above 3 g/t AuEq represents a robust underground gold target at current $4,348+ gold prices. The zone's proximity to the broader Duparquet Project — which hosts the historic Beattie deposits — and the fact it sits at relatively shallow depths accessible from underground development adds optionality to First Mining's resource growth thesis ahead of a resource update.

headline: BANNERMAN CLEARS LAST FUNDING HURDLE FOR ETANGO: CNNC LOCKED IN AS 45% JV PARTNER — NAMIBIA URANIUM FID TARGETED Q4 2026
source_name: Mining & Energy Namibia / Bannerman Energy Ltd. (ASX: BMN)
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) completed an AUD$124 million (USD$89 million) fully underwritten placement on September 10, 2026 — the last financing step required before a Final Investment Decision on the Etango uranium mine in Namibia, with settlement on September 15 and share allotment on September 16. Under the terms of the arrangement, CNNC Overseas Limited (CNOL) — the international arm of China's state-owned nuclear power operator — holds a 45% interest in the Etango joint venture, with Bannerman retaining 55%. CNOL has committed to purchase 60% of Etango's production under a cornerstone offtake agreement priced on arm's-length, market-based terms. The placement was priced at A$4.00 per share, a 5.4% discount to the prior close of A$4.23. Bannerman Executive Chairman Brando Munro stated the placement 'resolves the last funding hurdle for Bannerman as we move towards a Final Investment Decision on the Etango uranium mine.' FID is now targeted for Q4 2026, with full-scale construction commencement to follow. For uranium investors, the Etango transaction is structurally significant: a Chinese state nuclear operator committing as a 45% construction-funding JV partner — at $90+ uranium spot and $96.50 term prices — validates Namibia as a major new ex-Kazakh uranium supply source. The SPP opens September 18 and closes October 2, offering Australian retail investors a final opportunity to participate at the FID threshold.

headline: MARIMACA HITS 216m AT 1.0% Cu IN CHILE: PAMPA MEDINA SYSTEM CONFIRMED OVER 3km × 1.5km — BORNITE SULPHIDES DEEPENING
source_name: The Northern Miner / Marimaca Copper Corp. (TSX: MARI; ASX: MC2)
snippet: Marimaca Copper Corp. (TSX: MARI; ASX: MC2) reported September 8 that hole SPRD-15 at its Pampa Medina deposit in Chile's Antofagasta Region returned 216 metres grading 0.96% copper and 7.2 g/t silver from 466 metres downhole — including 62 metres at 2.2% copper and 21.5 g/t silver from 602 metres. This step-out pushed the copper-silver system approximately 300 metres beyond earlier holes, confirming continuity across a 3 km × 1.5 km drilled area. Mineralogy at depth transitions to sulphide-dominant assemblages: bornite, chalcopyrite, covellite, and chalcocite — copper sulphides with direct concentrator pathways rather than oxide leaching dependence. Near-surface oxide mineralization remains present above the sulphide zone. The stock was the TSX top gainer on September 8 on the news. For investors evaluating Chilean copper discoveries: a 216-metre continuous intercept averaging 1% copper at over 3 km of traced footprint in Chile's established Antofagasta copper belt — with high-grade 2.2% sub-intervals at depth — is a discovery at significant scale. Chile's established infrastructure, precedents for project development, and the Anglo-Teck merger background suggest Pampa Medina sits in a district increasingly relevant to major copper companies seeking resource pipeline replacements.

headline: SILVER47 WRAPS RED MOUNTAIN SUMMER DRILL: 197m CONTINUOUS SULFIDE AT 'SECOND CHANCE ZONE' IN ALASKA — ASSAYS STILL COMING
snippet: Silver47 Exploration Corp. (TSX-V: AGA) announced September 8 that it has completed 4,136 metres across 14 drill holes in its 2026 summer program at the high-grade silver and critical minerals Red Mountain Project in Alaska, 100 km south of Fairbanks. The headline visual result: hole SC26-003 at the new Second Chance Zone intersected 196.9 metres of continuous sulfide mineralization, including a cumulative 74 metres of semi-massive to massive sulfide. Four of five Second Chance holes hit the sulfide horizon over approximately 200 metres of strike and 150 metres down-dip, with surface mapping tracing the horizon for a potential 3 km strike extent — the zone remains fully open. All assays are pending. Executive Chairman Gary Thompson stated the visible sulfide mineralization at both Second Chance and the Dry Creek target 'demonstrates the strength of the Red Mountain Project.' The Bunker Hill Mining Corp. and Silver47 merger — which would create a 'Made in America' US Silver & Critical Minerals Champion combining Bunker Hill's Idaho Silver Valley mine with Silver47's Alaskan, Nevada, and New Mexico pipeline — was announced August 21, creating a completion context for the summer drill program. For silver investors: the combination of a 197-metre visual massive sulfide intercept in Alaska (assays pending) and the pending Bunker Hill merger positions Silver47's shareholders as beneficiaries of both an exploration re-rating if assays confirm grade and a corporate consolidation into an Idaho-Alaska US silver vehicle.

headline: 58 DAYS TO NOVEMBER 10: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE EXPIRES — REINSTATEMENT, SELECTIVE RESTART, OR EXTENSION?
snippet: China's 12-month suspension of its expanded rare earth export controls — covering extraterritorial provisions and additional heavy rare earth categories — expires November 10, 2026, now the most significant single calendar catalyst for ex-Chinese rare earth developers and their investors. The suspension was enacted as part of the Xi-Trump agreement that also rolled back some tariffs; the earlier April 2025 licensing regime on seven medium and heavy rare earth elements (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium) has remained fully enforced throughout. Three scenarios analysts are debating: (1) Extension of the suspension for another year — most likely if US-China trade relations hold; (2) Selective reinstatement targeting specific elements or end uses, particularly for materials used in defence applications; (3) Full reimposition of the October 2025 measures, which included extraterritorial provisions that could regulate controlled materials even after they leave Chinese territory. Context: China accounts for 69% of global rare earth mine production and processes 'up to 90%' globally. Germanium — under separate export controls since August 2023 — surged 10.04% in September's first tracking period while scandium fell 7.36%, illustrating how different individual elements respond to supply restriction signals. For investors in junior rare earth developers outside China — particularly companies targeting terbium, dysprosium, and neodymium-praseodymium in Australia, Canada, and the US — the November 10 expiry is a policy event that could either reset the risk premium or reaccelerate the strategic urgency that drove the sector's 2025 investment surge.

headline: SPROTT 'SEPTEMBER TO REMEMBER': FOMC BINARY PLUS BOJ — WHY GOLD'S STRUCTURAL FLOOR HOLDS ABOVE $4,200 REGARDLESS OF TUESDAY
snippet: Sprott Money's weekend market update for September 13-14 frames the dual central bank binary this week — the Federal Reserve rate decision on September 16 AND a Bank of Japan rate hike expected at its own September 17-18 meeting — as a setup that has not been adequately priced into gold and silver positioning. Gold gained 10.5% in August and silver 14.9% as institutions front-ran what they expected would be a FOMC inflection; September's inflation data partially reversed those gains. The Sprott analysis notes gold has held above $4,200 through the entire correction — a structural floor underpinned by 244 tonnes of central bank buying in Q1 2026 alone and six consecutive weeks of ETF inflows — arguing the September volatility is institutional positioning noise rather than a trend reversal. The Bank of Japan element adds another dimension: a BoJ hike-plus-hawkish signal from the Fed would strengthen the yen sharply against the dollar, historically supportive for gold as dollar strength is partially offset by yen-priced gold demand from Japanese investors unwinding carry trades. For silver, the $75-$76 level is flagged as the critical near-term technical test — a break above after the FOMC resolution would confirm silver's industrial deficit thesis over the rate-sensitivity thesis, consistent with the Silver Institute's projected sixth consecutive annual deficit of 46.3 million ounces for 2026.

headline: GOLD SELLOFF OR BREAKOUT AFTER SEPT 16? VERMEULEN LAYS OUT THE FORK: $8,000 BULL CONTINUATION OR $3,600 BEFORE THE REAL ADVANCE
source_name: Sprott Money Ltd. / Chris Vermeulen (Technical Traders)
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen's September 2026 analysis for Sprott Money presents gold's post-FOMC path as a genuine fork in the road rather than a one-sided setup. His two primary scenarios: (1) A sustained base at current levels ($4,200–$4,400) followed by a multi-year advance toward the $8,000 area — his bull case — driven by dollar reserve erosion, fiscal deficit expansion, and central bank accumulation continuing beyond the Fed cycle; (2) A decline toward approximately $3,600 before the larger multi-year advance begins — his bear case — triggered by a more aggressive Fed dot plot that forces institutional hands to reduce metal exposure during a multi-month consolidation. Vermeulen's technical indicators show short-term bullish but long-term cautionary signals simultaneously, describing 2026 as 'wildly volatile' and warning retail investors against binary event positioning. For silver, the $75–76 resistance zone is the level that separates continuation of the August momentum from a deeper reset toward $58. The analysis is notable for its intellectual honesty: at $4,348 gold entering the most important Federal Reserve meeting since the 2022 cycle began, both outcomes are credible, and Vermeulen explicitly argues against taking a leveraged view either direction through the event. For junior mining investors, the $3,600 scenario implies GDX and GDXJ testing their June 2026 support levels — a 20-30% drawdown from August peaks — before resuming; the $8,000 scenario implies the current correction is already over.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY EXTENDS ATLAS AND SALOON EAST AT PLS: 12.5m AT 1.8% eU3O8 IN HIGH-GRADE SASKATCHEWAN URANIUM BELT
source_name: PLS Exploration Ltd. / Paladin Energy Ltd. (ASX: PDN; TSX: PDN)
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX: PDN; TSX: PDN) released exploration results on September 2 from its Patterson Lake South (PLS) Project in Saskatchewan, Canada — advancing the Atlas and Saloon East discoveries discovered in 2024-2025 and extending mineralization beyond the current R1515W Mineral Resource at the Triple R deposit. The headline intercept from drill hole PLS26-782 returned 42.1 metres of total composite mineralization including 12.5 metres grading 1.8% eU3O8. The Atlas discovery sits in the Saloon Trend south of, and broadly parallel with, the Triple R deposit — a high-grade unconformity-type uranium deposit that defines the PLS project's resource base. Both Atlas and Saloon East were made through systematic step-out testing of geophysical anomalies that the 2025 discovery program identified. For uranium investors: the Patterson Lake South project in the Athabasca Basin — the world's highest-grade uranium district — is advancing multiple discovery fronts simultaneously, with Bannerman Energy (Etango, Namibia), Boss Energy (Honeymoon, South Australia), and now Paladin (PLS, Saskatchewan) all moving toward major production milestones as uranium spot holds near $90/lb and term contracts price at 18-year highs of $96.50/lb. The Atlas and Saloon East continuations add potential resource scale to PLS above and beyond the already-advanced Triple R deposit, which hosts the project's primary resource base.

headline: CAPITAL SHIFTS FROM BATTERY METALS: GLOBAL MINING SPENDING REDIRECTS TO COPPER, GOLD AND URANIUM AS LITHIUM EXPLORATION SLOWS
source_name: Mining South East Europe / IEA Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
snippet: Analysis drawing on the IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 and sector capital allocation data shows a definitive rotation in mining exploration and development spending in 2026: capital is flowing toward copper, gold, and uranium at the expense of early-stage battery metal exploration — particularly lithium, nickel, and cobalt. The shift reflects a reality that has been building since late 2024: lithium carbonate prices in China fell to CNY 143,000 per tonne in September (the lowest in nearly one month) even as CATL's Jianxiawo permit revocation removed a major supply source, because Australian producers — led by Core Lithium restarting Finniss and Mineral Resources rebooting Bald Hill — are adding supply at scale simultaneously. The structural story: at $65/oz silver, $14,000+/t copper, and $90+/lb uranium, those sectors generate returns that can support new exploration budgets. Lithium at CNY 143,000-160,000/t ($20-22K USD) supports production for operating assets but makes greenfield exploration economics marginal for anything other than the highest-grade, lowest-capex deposits. For retail investors holding battery metals exploration names: the de-rating of early-stage battery metals is a capital allocation story, not a demand story. Global lithium demand from EVs and energy storage is still projected to double by 2030, but excess supply from restarted Australian assets and Chinese domestic production is absorbing current demand growth faster than the market expected. The exploration-stage companies most likely to recover first are those with resources large enough to survive into the next price cycle, in jurisdictions with established infrastructure, and with management teams who can extend cash runway without dilutive equity issuance.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: EVOLUTION MINING EXPANDS COPPER PIPELINE WITH CARNABY RESOURCES DEAL — ERNEST HENRY GROWTH THESIS CONFIRMED
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlights Evolution Mining's (ASX: EVN) agreement to acquire Carnaby Resources for approximately A$213 million — a copper bolt-on deal that is the week's key M&A signal for gold-copper producers. The transaction, under a Scheme of Arrangement, incorporates the Greater Duchess copper-gold project near Evolution's existing Ernest Henry Operations in Queensland's Cloncurry copper-gold district. Greater Duchess is expected to deliver approximately 10,000 tonnes per year of additional copper production by leveraging Ernest Henry's latent mill capacity and existing infrastructure — a capital-efficient expansion model that avoids greenfield development costs. The combined tenement package also expands Evolution's exploration footprint across the Cloncurry district, adding multiple priority exploration targets. Shareholder and regulatory approvals are pending with a scheme meeting targeted for late October or early November 2026, and completion expected by mid-November. For investors, the GoldSeek SWOT assessment frames the deal as a 'Strength' event: a quality gold producer securing copper growth at Ernest Henry during a structural copper bull market, using mill capacity that was otherwise underutilized, at a price that values Greater Duchess at roughly $21 per tonne of projected annual copper production — a metric the market has historically re-rated upward as feasibility work advances. Evolution joins Equinox Gold (which completed the Orla Mining acquisition July 31, creating North America's new senior gold producer at ~1.1 million oz/yr) as the gold sector's most active corporate consolidators in the second half of 2026.
